s1.syndrome_frame: Rapidly progressive gait disturbance with spinal cord compression
salient_findings: Decreased sensation from the T3 dermatome downward
Clonus and hyperreflexia in the lower extremities
Diffusely enhancing lesion centered at T1 with near-circumferential epidural extension on MRI
key_facts: 1-week history of rapidly progressive gait disturbance
No back pain, fevers, night sweats, or weight loss
No history of smoking or known malignancy
Full strength throughout all extremities
Decreased sensation from the T3 dermatome downward
Four beats of clonus bilaterally
Hyperreflexia in the lower extremities
Profound ataxia
Expansile bony lesion of the T1 vertebral body with extension into the left pedicle and posterior elements on CT
No evidence of primary malignancy on CT scans of the chest, abdomen, and pelvis
Laboratory studies, including inflammatory markers, were within normal limits

shortlist.label: Chordoma
shortlist.why_kept: Expansile bony lesion of the T1 vertebral body with extension into the left pedicle and posterior elements

shortlist.label: Multiple myeloma
shortlist.why_kept: Rapidly progressive neurological decline with spinal cord compression and bony lesion

shortlist.label: Plasmacytoma
shortlist.why_kept: Solitary bony lesion with spinal cord compression and no evidence of primary malignancy

shortlist.label: Hemangioma
shortlist.why_kept: Expansile bony lesion with epidural extension causing spinal cord compression

shortlist.label: Giant cell tumor
shortlist.why_kept: Bony lesion with aggressive features and spinal cord compression

raw.rationale: The expansile bony lesion of the T1 vertebral body with extension into the left pedicle and posterior elements, along with the patient's rapidly progressive neurological decline and lack of evidence of primary malignancy, is most consistent with a chordoma, which is a rare bone tumor that can cause spinal cord compression.

rejected.label: Multiple myeloma
rejected.why: Typically presents with systemic symptoms such as bone pain, fevers, night sweats, and weight loss, which are absent in this patient

rejected.label: Plasmacytoma
rejected.why: Usually presents with a solitary lesion and may have systemic symptoms or abnormal laboratory studies, which are not present in this case

rejected.label: Hemangioma
rejected.why: Typically a benign vascular lesion that does not usually cause rapid neurological decline or expansile bony lesions

rejected.label: Giant cell tumor
rejected.why: More commonly occurs in the epiphyseal region of long bones and is less likely to cause the described spinal cord compression and neurological symptoms
